message:
Thanks, Elvera, and it's good to hear from you again. I've fixed the html so the links work, and I'm (as always) grateful for all the work that you're doing against the ugly [arrogance,](http://www.t-netix.com/aboutus_default.asp)[condescension](http://www.t-netix.com/), and [avarice](http://www.higcapital.com/) of corporate mouthpieces like "Power Corrupts" and "MAN" (see comments above).

Another thing people can do is vote with their wallets and work to discourage unethical investing: [contact](http://www.higcapital.com/contact_us.html) H.I.G. Capital and let them know you're disgusted that they fund companies like T-Netix and Securus. If you own stock in or benefit from endowments from [organizations like](http://www.higcapital.com/investors.html) Credit Suisse First Boston, Wachovia, Goldman Sachs, MIT, Verizon, or Yale, talk to them about the moral taint that association with H.I.G. and T-Netix and Securus gives them.

H.I.G. profits from T-Netix and Securus. T-Netix and Securus reap private profits from your misery and the misery of your loved ones. But the public taxes you pay support and condone this misery: if you've got a loved one in jail, not only is that loved one repaying a debt to society, but also -- via  extortionate rates from T-Netix and Securus -- lining the pockets of the wealthiest people in this country.

Maybe, nine years ago,  your younger brother did something incredibly stupid. (I'd like to meet a single person who *hasn't* done something incredibly stupid.) Maybe, in the interim, he's tutored inmates who couldn't read, helped inmates get their GEDs, and so contributed to a reduction in the rate of recidivism. But the state where he's incarcerated collects taxes, puts a portion of those taxes into the prison budget, and the prison system contracts with T-Netix -- giving them a nice, fat bit of money to run the phones -- and then what does T-Netix do? They charge extortionate rates (compare them to a calling card sometime), because they can. So, in effect, state governments  are taking kickbacks in order to give private companies like T-Netix the opportunity to reach into your wallets.

And so the rich get richer off the backs of the poor.
